description: This chart depicts the distribution of problems categorized by difficulty – easy, medium, and hard – and based on correctness with and without knowledge settings under a Zero-Shot condition. Each difficulty level is represented by a separate pie chart, with each chart containing four slices. The “easy” chart shows slices labeled “N+K+” in teal, occupying 55.4% of the chart, “N-K+” in goldenrod, occupying 38.3%, “N-K-” in coral, occupying 4.6%, and “N+K-” in light orange, occupying 1.7%. The “medium” chart displays “N+K+” in teal at 58.8%, “N-K+” in goldenrod at 35.4%, “N-K-” in coral at 4.8% and “N+K-” in light orange at 1.0%. The “hard” chart features “N+K+” in teal at 37.3%, “N-K+” in goldenrod at 37.9%, “N-K-” in coral at 18.1%, and “N+K-” in light orange at 6.7%. A legend is included, associating the colors teal, goldenrod, coral, and light orange with the labels “N+K+”, “N-K+”, “N-K-”, and “N+K-” respectively. Percentage labels are displayed within each slice. The slices within each chart appear to be ordered clockwise from largest to smallest proportion.
